graded.case: graded or bent crystal (advanced): dE/E 0.10, peak 0.3

crystals.note: A crystal at one orientation diffracts one narrow band of a broad continuum; every other photon passes into the crystal and is attenuated there. Crystals turn photons by large angles (2 theta_B, tens of mrad) but only a percent-level share of a bremsstrahlung spectrum, so as heat shields they add absorber rather than remove it.

neutrons.note: Supermirrors (m up to about 6-8 today) and any layered structure down to atomic spacing reflect MeV neutrons only below about 0.1 mrad; hiding a 3 cm edge takes hundreds of metres to kilometres of mirror. Moderating a fast neutron first deposits its energy, which is the heat the optics was meant to avoid. Fast neutrons can only be avoided (geometry), shadowed (removal), or not made (fuel).

A_C_drawn_engine.note: Heat booked at full absorption of the non-reflected share (the 1.5 upper bracket for the bare engine); the 1.5 Compton-only lower bracket would scale every row by the same transport factor, so the reflected share is the result.

B_collimator.note: Without the collimator these photons leave with zero heat. Any structure placed in a free escape path adds heat; the gain is bounded by P/(2c) per engine even for loss-free optics.
